summary: Jambi stands under Indonesia's national framework, which the parent record carries in full. The sources identify no Jambi-specific signal: no provincial or district-level ordinance addressing same-sex conduct or gender expression, no local anti-discrimination protection, and no documented incident involving a trans person in the province. A trans visitor in Jambi therefore faces the national assessment without local modification, and no Jambi institution, regulation or enforcement practice altering it was found.
tangentialFactors: The Jambi material offers nothing to compare: no ranking of provinces by incidents, no contrast with neighbouring provinces, and no local turbulence is documented. National indicators in the sources, including opinion polling on homosexuality and enforcement operations carried out elsewhere in Indonesia, describe the country as a whole and are not attributable to Jambi.
localsOnly: Residents of Jambi live under the national framework with no provincial overlay. No local rule adds penalties or protections beyond national law, and no Jambi-level body, court or regulation providing redress on grounds of gender identity was identified in the sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Jambi's districts and municipalities have enacted morality or public-order ordinances of their own is unresolved. The sources surveyed are national in scope and contain no Jambi fieldwork, so an absence of recorded local rules is not confirmation that none exist.

No documented incident involving a trans or gender-nonconforming person in Jambi was located, and the sources do not establish whether this reflects an absence of incidents or an absence of reporting. Local police practice in Jambi, including any use of national morality provisions against private gatherings, is not sourced.
